witness_description: No witness. The claim fragment asserts that 'the remaining passengers C2 ∪ C3 on the left form an independent set', but supplies neither the graph (vertices/edges, or what adjacency between passengers means), nor the definitions of the classes C2 and C3, nor what 'remaining' and 'on the left' refer to. Any concrete instantiation would have to be invented, so no found witness could soundly refute the proof's actual claim.
refutation_explanation: Not applicable: the claim as quoted is not finitely refutable. It is a contingent assertion about specific sets C2, C3 produced by an unquoted construction in an unquoted graph. A deterministic demonstration sweep in test.py over all 8 graphs on 3 labelled vertices crossed with all 8 candidate designations of C2 ∪ C3 (64 exact, integer-only cases) shows both outcomes occur (45 independent, 19 not independent), confirming the truth value depends entirely on the missing definitions; this sweep is a soundness demonstration, not a counterexample search over the actual claim.
search_space: No sound search space exists for the fragment as given. Illustrative-only sweep executed: all 2^3 = 8 simple graphs on 3 labelled vertices x all 2^3 = 8 subsets designated as C2 ∪ C3 (64 pairs, fixed iteration order, exact integer arithmetic), used solely to demonstrate that the claim's truth is contingent on unsupplied data.
